sentences: I also read on forums some swear it stops the seizure from going any further, and there was one woman whose EEG showed fewer seizure discharges on the days she smoked.
But other people say THC vapes and concentrates brought their seizures on.
That matches what happened in rats that get the brief staring seizures called absence seizures: high-THC smoke gave them more of those seizures, while injected CBD cut the number about in half.
So the THC may be what makes cannabis go either way.

codex: The paragraph follows an orderly progression from anecdote to counterexample to experiment to tentative conclusion, which can feel model-polished beneath its conversational voice. These are weak stylistic cues; the paragraph alone cannot establish authorship.
haiku: The paragraph runs at even, similar sentence lengths and moves in a clean sequence of evidence, pivot, study, and tidy close, which reads like a polished summary more than someone working through what they found. The voice stays smooth and generic, with no hesitation or loose ends.
sonnet: The paragraph moves in a perfectly orderly sequence of claim, counterclaim, supporting evidence and resolving conclusion, with evenly sized sentences and no digression, so it reads as assembled to a logical template rather than thought through aloud. Its voice is evenly explanatory and never snags.
